description: Architectural DXF reverse engineering: simple 2-story 3D steel frame
message: Extract the structural grid and beam connectivity from the attached architectural floor-plan DXF and engineering specification, filter out walls, doors, windows, and furniture, build the spatial calculation model, and run static analysis. Use visible plan dimensions and topology; do not infer missing engineering information.
engineeringSpecification: Material Q345: E=206000 MPa, nu=0.3, density=7850 kg/m3, fy=345 MPa. Column members use section HW350x350 (H=350 mm, B=350 mm, tw=12 mm, tf=19 mm; A=0.01739 m2, Iy=0.000403 m4, Iz=0.000136 m4, J=0.00000863 m4, G=79000 MPa). Beam members use section HN500x200 (H=500 mm, B=200 mm, tw=10 mm, tf=16 mm; A=0.01143 m2, Iy=0.000502 m4, Iz=0.0000214 m4, J=0.00000124 m4, G=79000 MPa). Map the floor plan's source X/Y axes to global X/Y; create two stories in global Z, each 3.6 m high. Use fixed column bases and apply a global-Z downward 10 kN/m2 floor load on each story. Use SI units and the global-Z-up coordinate convention, do not add member self-weight, and analyze load combination ULS = 1 x D.
